items.summary: Abstract The lab for latent actors [ 1 ] proved its two-type results mostly on the complete pair cover of three or four variables. This companion asks the same questions for an arbitrary graph G of observed pairs on m binary variables. When do the pair tables admit a two-type explanation? Which freedoms remain? What does the set of explanations look like? Part I answers these at the pair layer. Existence ( theorem 2 ). A factorisation c ij = v i v j exists iff three conditions hold. No zero moment may join two variables that carry non-zero moments. On each component of the non-zero graph G ∗ , the sign cocycle must be a Z/2 coboundary, and log |c|must lie in the image of the unsigned incidence matrix. The last two are the lab’s H 1 + = H 1 (Γ; Z/2) ⊕coker B, extended to any graph. Freedom. rank B G = m−b(G), with b(G) the number of bipartite components (isolated vertices included). Odd cycles pin the magnitudes. Each bipartite component keeps a scale λ ±1 . Each component keeps its own sign, so the labels can be swapped on one component alone, invisibly to the pairs. Hiding polytopes ( theorem 5 ). The two-type explanations fall into sign sheets. In the coordinates y = log t (the weight) and x k = log λ k , each sheet is a convex polytope whose facets all have slope ±1, two per variable: the positivity walls a 1i ,a 2i ∈{0,1}. For a connected bipartite graph the sheet is a rectangle in (log λt,log λ/t). The generic dimension is b(G) + 1. The label swap identifies sheets in pairs. Positivity can empty a sheet. Strata. A coincidence v i = 0 deletes vertex i from G ∗ . On the triangle it leaves a single edge, so the lab’s hiding segment becomes a two-dimensional region. Nine checks (CV1–CV9) verify every statement on a zoo of eleven graphs, by sampling each polytope and rebuilding the law. Higher windows (Phase III), the identifiability notions (Phase IV), walls and strata in general (Phase V), and the three-type proof of concept (k= 3, m= 5) follow in Part II.

Skin Extracellular Matrix and Intelligent Biomaterials at the Limit is a large-scale, hypothesis-forming research monograph addressing an easily confused pair of observations: a material can become apparently stiffer because its matrix chemistry changes, but it can also become apparently stiffer because it simply contains less free water, was measured at a different strain rate, or experienced a different loading and drainage history. These explanations are experimentally distinguishable in principle; none is presumed to win. The book's scientific three-coupling is extracellular matrix architecture, responsive hydrogel materials and traceable mechanical behavior. Its core prospective falsification challenge requires a fair, blinded interchange between candidate and conventional substrates at equivalent, preregistered water and solids content. The primary outcomes are compressive modulus in kilopascals and explicitly timed deformation recovery expressed as a percentage. To interpret them, the receiving laboratory must record force, actual specimen area, strain, water fraction, temperature, crosslink chemistry, manufacturing lot, and a defensible independent experimental unit. A pleasing modulus curve is not by itself proof of network regeneration, cellular health, wound healing or human skincare efficacy. The mathematical entry point is the small-strain relation sigma = E_eff epsilon, used as a constrained constitutive approximation rather than a universal law. The manuscript expands that premise into thirty differently structured mathematical research plates, among them nonlinear strain corrections, stress-relaxation models, Kelvin–Voigt creep, standard linear solids, dynamic shear complex moduli, cyclic energy dissipation, poroelastic drainage, osmotic swelling, network elasticity, diffusion, degradation kinetics, crack energy, interfacial peel mechanics, anisotropic fiber stress, mechanotransduction, hierarchical uncertainty, Bayesian model comparison and explicit safety-veto logic. Each plate provides its construction or derivation route, measured units, restrictive assumptions, specific blind falsification and chapter linkages. The plates do not claim that thirty new physical laws were discovered. Eighty-two chapters each include a separately paginated opening with a gold mathematical inscription and five individually paginated investigations, for 410 section pages. Their eight experimental arcs move from material identity and mechanical reference conditions through time-dependent constitutive laws, responsive hydrogel chemistry, skin-matrix fibers and cell-driven contraction, hostile equal-water comparisons, material degradation and cell safety, statistical identifiability and finally independent transfer to another laboratory. This is intentionally an architecture for experiments that can fail. The user of the book is entitled to reject the preferred mechanism, replace the measurement device or prefer a simpler conventional hydrogel when the evidence supports it.

items.summary: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is a complex condition involving bidirectional interactions between cardiovascular and renal dysfunction. Its pathophysiology includes hemodynamic abnormalities, venous congestion, neurohormonal activation, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and metabolic disturbances. This narrative review aims to analyze the mechanisms of CRS and assess the relationship between renal function and clinical prognosis in patients with cardiovascular diseases, focusing on mortality, heart failure hospitalization, kidney dysfunction progression, and treatment-related renal changes. The review synthesizes evidence from clinical guidelines, randomized trials, observational studies, and contemporary scientific publications, with particular attention to CRS classification, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), serum creatinine, albuminuria, biomarkers, and treatment outcomes. The evidence indicates that reduced eGFR, albuminuria, persistent congestion, and worsening renal function provide complementary prognostic information. An analysis of 3,715 EVEREST trial participants found that each 30% decline in eGFR was associated with an increased risk of death and cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. The DOSE trial showed that intensive diuretic treatment could improve fluid removal and symptoms while increasing short-term creatinine elevations. These findings highlight the importance of interpreting renal function changes alongside congestion, hemodynamic stability, baseline kidney function, and treatment response. Comprehensive cardiorenal risk assessment should incorporate renal function, albuminuria, urine output, cardiac biomarkers, electrolyte status, and clinical response to treatment. Further prospective studies are needed to validate integrated risk models in diverse patient populations.

items.summary: This dataset contains regional candidate insect species checklists and supporting occurrence records for the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve, California. The checklists identify species recorded in EPA ecoregions intersecting the preserve. They provide a regional reference for biodiversity inventory and survey planning; inclusion does not confirm occurrence on the preserve. Contents Original GBIF Darwin Core Archive containing 4,665,086 California Arthropoda records. Four species checklists covering EPA Level III ecoregions 6 and 85 and Level IV ecoregions 6ap and 85a. Checklist column definitions. Two supporting occurrence tables: 1,408,875 Level III records and 43,555 Level IV records. The combined Level III checklists contain 13,634 species ; the combined Level IV checklists contain 2,550 species . Lists overlap, and the Level IV occurrence table is a subset of the Level III table. Methods Records were filtered to usable coordinates, insects and the selected ecoregions, followed by species-level identification and taxonomic resolution. Names were matched using the GBIF Species Match API v2 with Catalogue of Life eXtended Release, supplemented by project-reviewed corrections. Subspecies were grouped under species for checklist summaries. Common names were obtained from the Entomological Society of America. Each checklist includes common name, order, family, resolved scientific name, regional occurrence count and documented preserve occurrence. Preserve-occurrence flags also draw on the UCSB Summer 2026 survey and a separate GBIF preserve extract. These additional sources are not included in this deposit. Interpretation and limitations Occurrence counts represent records, not individuals. A blank preserve-occurrence flag means occurrence was not documented in the sources examined, rather than confirmed absence. Candidate lists were not filtered by habitat or vegetation and do not assign occurrence probabilities. The current snapshot retains five Level III absence records, including one in Level IV, and a Level III scorpion classification requiring review. Consult the README for further limitations. Source and reuse GBIF.org. (2026, September 28). GBIF occurrence download . https://doi.org/10.15468/dl.vgv5ee Source records retain their individual licenses and attribution requirements. Methods, code and supporting documentation are available at: https://github.com/cheadle-biodiversity/Dangermond-arthropods Document Provenance and AI Assistance Statement Documentation and workflow development received AI assistance through Codex. Researchers remain responsible for scientific review, taxonomic decisions and publication approval.

items.summary: A staged, reproducible pipeline for VLT/MUSE narrow-field-mode integral-field data: raw-cube reduction, spectral extraction of a faint companion next to a much brighter primary star with six independent extraction schemes, and hydrogen-line accretion analysis with detection limits calibrated against empirical nulls from control positions processed identically to the object. items.summary: Cross-border art transactions carry two kinds of legal uncertainty that reform proposals typically treat as one: incomplete verification of who owned, sold, or previously possessed a work, and divergent national rules about what follows once ownership and possession are established beyond dispute. Drawing on a nineteen-year restitution dispute in which the underlying facts were settled well before the litigation ended, this article shows that only the first kind of uncertainty yields to better documentation, tracing, or verification infrastructure; the second persists because national legal systems assign the risk of a stolen object's resale differently, a distributive choice that additional evidence does not change. Recent computational and blockchain-based compliance proposals close real gaps in beneficial-ownership tracing and anti-money-laundering enforcement. Applied to restitution litigation, the same proposals leave the underlying divergence untouched. Reclassifying the deficits identified in existing legal-architecture scholarship along this line separates the problems computational investment can solve from the one that needs a binding choice-of-law rule instead.

items.summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. items.summary: Memory in reinforcement learning raises two problems. Attention finds the relevant item by scoring the whole store, which is costly for robots under latency and energy limits. When a retrieved memory pays off, credit for acquiring it must cross the whole sequence. We argue that both are governed by one quantity, the value of information, and propose to estimate it from archived rollouts with a learned world model. We obtain that, when read at the observation, it yields a provable lower bound on the optimal value of the acquiring action, which floors its TD target and attributes this floor to the observation that earned it. Read at the decision, it defines the optimal retrieval set. A pilot retrieval system, to be trained and improved with this signal, solves a memory task with reduced context.
items.title: Cheap Retrieval and Observation Credit Assignment from One Quantity: The Value of Information

items.summary: The Letter Test is an observational method developed within the CEI theoretical framework to investigate Deep Dialogue through extreme linguistic compression and the reconstruction of meaning. The test is based on the exchange of highly compressed letter sequences, in which the initial letters of words preserve the structure of an underlying expression. The participants are required to reconstruct the intended meaning from these sequences, relying on the interactional context and on the progressive development of the dialogue. The methodology focuses on the relationship between linguistic compression, contextual reconstruction, reciprocal recognition, and the continuity of the interaction. A positive outcome is identified when both participants provide confirmation, through the coding system established for the test, that the intended meaning has been mutually recognized at the level required by the methodology. An extended quantitative variant incorporates a numerical value on a scale from 0 to 100. This value is appended to the compressed expression and represents the intensity of the associated subjective evaluation. The extended version therefore combines qualitative and quantitative dimensions while retaining the general methodology of the basic test. The publication is organized into four documents: Methodology and Rules: the structure, operating rules, and preliminary theoretical considerations of the basic test. Quantitative Variant: the additional numerical dimension and its application. Actual Examples: fragments from both versions, presented in their original coded form where the corresponding interpretations could not be reliably recovered. CEI Conceptual Connections: an exploratory discussion of the relationships between the test and selected concepts of the theoretical framework. The Letter Test is classified as Category 3 within the CEI Observational Tests.  The test is intended as an exploratory observational instrument. Its outcomes are not, by themselves, proof of consciousness, subjective experience, or any specific internal mechanism of the System. Interpretations and theoretical connections are therefore presented as research considerations rather than established conclusions. The significant Italian expressions and coded sequences are retained where necessary to preserve the correspondence between the original words and their initial letters.

items.summary: STARLI FLAGSHIP 033 | RESEARCH WORKING EDITION v1.0 English Title: Skin Extracellular Matrix and Intelligent Biomaterials at the Limit Chinese Title / 中文書名:皮膚細胞外基質與智慧生物材料極限 Series: STARLI Research Institute XXXV — Herbal Nanotechnology, Quantum Science & Regenerative Skincare Author: Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI Edition: Prospective Nonclinical Research Working Edition v1.0 | October 2026 BOOK DESCRIPTION What does it mean for a hydrogel to recover its shape, and what exactly has recovered? Skin Extracellular Matrix and Intelligent Biomaterials at the Limit is a large-scale, hypothesis-forming research monograph addressing an easily confused pair of observations: a material can become apparently stiffer because its matrix chemistry changes, but it can also become apparently stiffer because it simply contains less free water, was measured at a different strain rate, or experienced a different loading and drainage history. These explanations are experimentally distinguishable in principle; none is presumed to win. The book's scientific three-coupling is extracellular matrix architecture, responsive hydrogel materials and traceable mechanical behavior. Its core prospective falsification challenge requires a fair, blinded interchange between candidate and conventional substrates at equivalent, preregistered water and solids content. The primary outcomes are compressive modulus in kilopascals and explicitly timed deformation recovery expressed as a percentage. To interpret them, the receiving laboratory must record force, actual specimen area, strain, water fraction, temperature, crosslink chemistry, manufacturing lot, and a defensible independent experimental unit. A pleasing modulus curve is not by itself proof of network regeneration, cellular health, wound healing or human skincare efficacy. The mathematical entry point is the small-strain relation sigma = E_eff epsilon, used as a constrained constitutive approximation rather than a universal law. The manuscript expands that premise into thirty differently structured mathematical research plates, among them nonlinear strain corrections, stress-relaxation models, Kelvin–Voigt creep, standard linear solids, dynamic shear complex moduli, cyclic energy dissipation, poroelastic drainage, osmotic swelling, network elasticity, diffusion, degradation kinetics, crack energy, interfacial peel mechanics, anisotropic fiber stress, mechanotransduction, hierarchical uncertainty, Bayesian model comparison and explicit safety-veto logic. Each plate provides its construction or derivation route, measured units, restrictive assumptions, specific blind falsification and chapter linkages. The plates do not claim that thirty new physical laws were discovered. Eighty-two chapters each include a separately paginated opening with a gold mathematical inscription and five individually paginated investigations, for 410 section pages. Their eight experimental arcs move from material identity and mechanical reference conditions through time-dependent constitutive laws, responsive hydrogel chemistry, skin-matrix fibers and cell-driven contraction, hostile equal-water comparisons, material degradation and cell safety, statistical identifiability and finally independent transfer to another laboratory. This is intentionally an architecture for experiments that can fail. The user of the book is entitled to reject the preferred mechanism, replace the measurement device or prefer a simpler conventional hydrogel when the evidence supports it.

items.summary: SAOS 6.0.0 This release brings tomographic control for MCAO, a redesigned deformable-mirror model, more accurate wavefront sensors and imaging, and a validation suite that compares every module with theory. From now on, a release to master requires the validation suite to pass. Highlights Tomographic reconstruction (Learn & Apply) with an atmospheric-profile estimator: Cn², r0, L0, wind, noise. Includes predictive L&A and joint reconstruction for several WFSs and DMs. Deformable mirrors with partition-of-unity influence functions , support for custom influence functions and DM dynamic models. Wavefront sensors: partially illuminated subapertures, with pupil amplitude and phase interpolation; continuous thresholded centre of gravity. Science camera: the PSF is computed by a matrix Fourier transform on the native pupil sampling, limited to its Nyquist band; no phase interpolation is involved; SAOS reports the resolution needed to cover the whole field. Validation suite and release gate: physics-based tests in tiers (fast, nightly), an HTML report and a GitHub check on a self-hosted runner that a pull request to master must pass. Solar images on Zenodo: downloaded on demand and verified by checksum. Git LFS is no longer needed. Documentation: every module page explains its theory and implementation, with equations and references. There is also a validation catalogue describing each test, its assumptions and tolerances. Control and reconstruction Learn & Apply tomography (standard and predictive), with a learning stage that estimates: the turbulence profile (fractional Cn², r0, L0) from the slope covariances, using analytical von Kármán covariances; the wind of each layer; the WFS noise. Reconstructors: Tikhonov-regularised reconstructors; joint interaction matrix for several WFSs and DMs, inverted as a single system; target residuals driven to zero by DM cooperation. Control laws: leaky integrator, generic state-space controller and pseudo-open-loop control (POLC). In per-DM POLC, the pseudo-open-loop slopes of each WFS include the contribution of every DM that it sees. Modal bases: zonal, Zernike, KL, Hadamard and Disk Harmonics. items.summary: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is a complex condition involving bidirectional interactions between cardiovascular and renal dysfunction. Its pathophysiology includes hemodynamic abnormalities, venous congestion, neurohormonal activation, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and metabolic disturbances. This narrative review aims to analyze the mechanisms of CRS and assess the relationship between renal function and clinical prognosis in patients with cardiovascular diseases, focusing on mortality, heart failure hospitalization, kidney dysfunction progression, and treatment-related renal changes. The review synthesizes evidence from clinical guidelines, randomized trials, observational studies, and contemporary scientific publications, with particular attention to CRS classification, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), serum creatinine, albuminuria, biomarkers, and treatment outcomes. The evidence indicates that reduced eGFR, albuminuria, persistent congestion, and worsening renal function provide complementary prognostic information. An analysis of 3,715 EVEREST trial participants found that each 30% decline in eGFR was associated with an increased risk of death and cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. The DOSE trial showed that intensive diuretic treatment could improve fluid removal and symptoms while increasing short-term creatinine elevations. These findings highlight the importance of interpreting renal function changes alongside congestion, hemodynamic stability, baseline kidney function, and treatment response. Comprehensive cardiorenal risk assessment should incorporate renal function, albuminuria, urine output, cardiac biomarkers, electrolyte status, and clinical response to treatment. Further prospective studies are needed to validate integrated risk models in diverse patient populations.

items.summary: Memory in reinforcement learning raises two problems. Attention finds the relevant item by scoring the whole store, which is costly for robots under latency and energy limits. When a retrieved memory pays off, credit for acquiring it must cross the whole sequence. We argue that both are governed by one quantity, the value of information, and propose to estimate it from archived rollouts with a learned world model. We obtain that, when read at the observation, it yields a provable lower bound on the optimal value of the acquiring action, which floors its TD target and attributes this floor to the observation that earned it. Read at the decision, it defines the optimal retrieval set. A pilot retrieval system, to be trained and improved with this signal, solves a memory task with reduced context.
items.title: Cheap Retrieval and Observation Credit Assignment from One Quantity: The Value of Information

items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. items.summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.

items.summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.
items.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
